scope_note: MAP run on src/engine/linker (primary, authored fresh) + compiler pilot findings folded in (secondary, read cross-branch from hardening-ii-compiler). MAP recovers truth and routes; it does not fix. No production behavior changed by this run.
status_vocab: open | routed | remediated | accepted. 'routed' = a home exists (background task / branch); 'accepted' = verified, no remediation needed (informational).
rollup_rule: Dashboard counts are DERIVED from these findings by scripts/pdd-atlas-rollup.mjs — never hand-typed. openRisksHigh = risk∧open∧severity:high; openRisksTotal = risk∧open; footgunsOpen = footgun∧open; silentFailuresReal = silent-failure∧open∧classification:real; coverageGaps = coverage-gap∧open.

findings.title: Linker is tested but never mutation-graded — test adequacy unknown
findings.falsifiable_condition: Stryker scoped to src/engine/linker reports surviving mutants that are weak tests (a behavior no test pins), not merely dead code.
findings.evidence: stryker.config.json mutate-globs cover src/engine/compiler/** ONLY (stryker.config.json:9-13); the linker has 36 GREEN tests across 15 files (npx vitest run src/engine/linker, 1.47s) but 0% of them are mutation-graded. The compiler pilot showed even a ~93%-mutation subsystem still hid a domain-spanning survivor; an un-graded 36-test suite over a branch-dense data pipeline almost certainly hides weak tests.
findings.blast_radius: Linker is the LIVE content pipeline: ModuleLinker.linkProject is the active-cartridge loader (src/engine/workspace/WorkspaceService.ts:49,93) and menu config loader (src/ui/runtime/ambient/loadMenuAmbientConfig.ts:14). A weak test lets a content-loading bug ship wrong game data silently.

findings.title: normalizeBpInput first-entry heuristic can ship the WRONG blueprint with no error
findings.falsifiable_condition: A .bp fragment with an ambiguous multi-key shape (no top-level id, multiple nested entries) links to a different blueprint than authored, producing NO LinkerValidationError.
findings.evidence: normalizeBpInput runs on EVERY .bp parse (semanticParser.ts:75). On ambiguous shapes it falls back to 'first entry': `entries.find(([key]) => key === raw.id)?.[1] ?? entries[0]?.[1]` (normalizeBpInput.ts:10) and `Object.values(raw)[0]` (normalizeBpInput.ts:21). A wrong guess produces a schema-valid blueprint that compiles and ships — the failure is data-shaped, not exception-shaped.

findings.title: .cave validation schema has drifted from SysConfig: `pointer` unauthorable, `swarm`/`understanding` land untyped
findings.falsifiable_condition: (a) A .cave file with a top-level `pointer` block throws LinkerValidationError (the schema is .strict() and omits `pointer`). (b) A .cave file with `swarm` or `understanding` succeeds and those keys land in runtime.config even though SysConfig does not model them.
findings.evidence: The .cave fragment is TYPED `Partial<z.infer<typeof SysConfigSchema>>` (semanticParser.types.ts:8) but VALIDATED by a separate hand-written .strict() object literal (semanticParser.ts:25-41). Key-set diff vs SysConfigSchema (src/data/schemas/v2/config.ts:15-29): .cave adds `swarm`,`understanding` (not in SysConfig); .cave omits `pointer` (present in SysConfig). The two are maintained independently and have already diverged.

findings.title: BlueprintV2 type is narrower than its own schema, then cast unchecked into the compiler's Blueprint
findings.falsifiable_condition: A `components`-form blueprint (valid per BlueprintV2Schema) either loses data through link→namespace→serialize, or reaches CompilerService.compile in a shape the compiler mishandles — neither caught by a type error because the boundary is `as unknown as`.
findings.evidence: BlueprintV2Schema accepts `components` and `_editor` (blueprintV2Schema.ts:21-22) that the BlueprintV2 TYPE omits (types.ts:28-44). compileRuntimeBlueprints then bridges linker BlueprintV2 → compiler Blueprint with a double cast `as unknown as` (moduleLinkerRuntime.ts:49-51), so the seam is asserted, not verified.

findings.title: Manifest `files` defaults to [] — a typo'd manifest key silently yields an empty cartridge
findings.falsifiable_condition: A manifest.json that is valid JSON but spells the key wrong (e.g. `{"file":[...]}`) links to an empty RuntimeCartridge with no error or warning.
findings.evidence: ManifestSchema = z.object({ files: z.array(z.string()).default([]) }) (ModuleLinker.ts:12). A parseable manifest missing `files` validates (default []) and linkProject iterates zero files, returning an empty-but-default cartridge with no trace (ModuleLinker.ts:84-99).

findings.title: collisionDetectorExtras.ts — latent bug: sampler-target/state-key collision is unreachable
findings.falsifiable_condition: Already falsified and locked: collisionDetector.property.test.ts P3c is an `it.fails` documenting the unreachable branch; fixing the bug auto-flips it green.
findings.evidence: Source: docs/hardening-ii-compiler-pilot.md (read cross-branch from hardening-ii-compiler). nonSamplerState = stateKeys − samplerTargets, then membership is tested on a value that is always a samplerTarget, so the collision can never trigger. Contradicts ph13 §2.2 l.150.

findings.title: storageCompilerReconciler.ts — ~16 mutation survivors are dead code (cleanup, no behavior change)
findings.falsifiable_condition: Deleting the cond4 passive-effect predicate (l.103-110) and the runtime-dead `state?.[key]` reads (l.65,68) leaves the full compiler suite GREEN and the mutation score unchanged-or-higher.
findings.evidence: Source: docs/hardening-ii-compiler-pilot.md. The cond4 passive-effect predicate (l.103-110) is subsumed by the source-prefix check (l.92-100); `state?.[key]` (l.65,68) is runtime-dead. ~16/17 survivors on this module are dead code, not weak tests — no test can kill dead code.

findings.title: Gatekeeper depends on ModuleLinker but never links — the dependency is a method-presence guard
findings.appearance: Gatekeeper(linker: ModuleLinker) reads as a validator that links/compiles the project to validate it.
findings.reality: validatePayload only checks `typeof this.linker.linkProject === 'function'` (Gatekeeper.ts:52) and otherwise never calls it. Validation is pure: ModuleCartridgeSchema.safeParse + a recursive FQ-ref collection (collectRefs) against existing ids. The real linking is done elsewhere (WorkspaceService.ts:49). The injected linker is a guard, not a collaborator.

findings.title: `.cave` fragment is typed Partial<SysConfig> but validated by a divergent hand-written schema
findings.appearance: SemanticFragment kind 'cave' is `data: Partial<z.infer<typeof SysConfigSchema>>` (semanticParser.types.ts:8) — i.e. 'a partial SysConfig, governed by SysConfigSchema'.
findings.reality: Validation uses a SEPARATE .strict() object literal (semanticParser.ts:25-41) whose key-set differs from SysConfigSchema: it accepts `swarm`/`understanding` (absent from SysConfig) and rejects `pointer` (present in SysConfig). The type is a promise the validator does not keep.

findings.title: A .bp registry KEY is not the blueprint id — an explicit `id` field overrides it, and a pre-namespaced id skips namespacing
findings.appearance: A .bp file is `{ "<id>": { ...blueprint } }`, so the map key is read as the blueprint's id and `namespace::key` is the resolved id.
findings.reality: namespaceBlueprints prefers a non-empty `blueprint.id` over the registry key (linkerUtils.ts:28-32); resolveId leaves any id already containing '::' un-namespaced (utils/namespaces.ts:2). So the resolved id can differ from the visible key, and namespacing can be silently bypassed.

findings.title: deepMergeObjects: `null` ERASES the base subtree and arrays REPLACE wholesale (not merge)
findings.appearance: 'deepMerge' implies recursive combine — overlaying config/draft/assets fragments accretes values.
findings.reality: An override value of `null` returns null, deleting the entire base subtree (deepMerge.ts:14); an override array is cloned and replaces the base array entirely (deepMerge.ts:15); only `undefined` is skipped (deepMerge.ts:13,21). The merge is destructive at null/array boundaries.

findings.title: compileRuntimeBlueprints bridges linker→compiler types with a double `as unknown as` cast
findings.appearance: compileRuntimeBlueprints reads as a typed step: BlueprintV2 in, compiled BlueprintV2 out.
findings.reality: It casts each BlueprintV2 to the compiler's Blueprint via `compiler.compile(blueprint as unknown as Blueprint)` and back `as unknown as` (moduleLinkerRuntime.ts:49-51). The two blueprint types are structurally different (flat component slots vs a `components` record) and the seam is asserted, never verified.

findings.title: BlueprintV2Schema accepts fields (`components`, `_editor`) that the BlueprintV2 type omits
findings.appearance: BlueprintV2Schema (validation) and BlueprintV2 (type) describe the same blueprint shape.
findings.reality: The schema allows `components: z.record(...)` and `_editor` (blueprintV2Schema.ts:21-22); the type has neither (types.ts:28-44). A `components`-form blueprint validates but is invisible to the type and to code that reads BlueprintV2's flat slots.

findings.title: Unsupported file extension in the manifest is skipped with only a warn
findings.rationale: readFragment logs `logger.warn('[Linker] Ignored unsupported file type: …')` and returns null, dropping the file from the build (ModuleLinker.ts:71-74). It has a visible trace (warn), so it is benign — but the trace is warn-level and was observed firing for a typo'd `flow.cvs` in CompileProject.system.test.ts, so a mis-extensioned content file is omitted while the build still 'succeeds'.

findings.title: Blueprint id collision across fragments is overridden with only a debug log
findings.rationale: mergeRegistry calls onCollision(id) which routes to logger.debug('[Linker] Blueprint override: …') (registryMerge.ts:18, moduleLinkerRuntime.ts:42), then the later blueprint overrides the earlier by id. This is intended mod-layering and has a trace, so benign — but the trace is debug-level (the lowest visibility), so an accidental id clash reads as a silent override in any non-debug run.

findings.title: normalizeBpInput silently picks the first entry on an ambiguous .bp shape
findings.rationale: On a .bp shape it cannot disambiguate, normalizeBpInput falls back to `entries[0]?.[1]` (line 10) / `Object.values(raw)[0]` (line 21). A wrong pick yields a schema-valid blueprint that links and compiles with no error — the wrong content ships untraced. This is the data-shaped silent failure the exception-seed sweep cannot find.

findings.title: Typo'd manifest key yields an empty cartridge with no trace
findings.rationale: ManifestSchema defaults `files` to [] (ModuleLinker.ts:12). A parseable manifest with the wrong key validates, linkProject loads zero fragments, and returns a default-but-empty RuntimeCartridge with no error or warning (ModuleLinker.ts:84-99) — indistinguishable from an intentionally empty project.

findings.title: normalizeBpInput.ts — branch-dense, 0% mutation-graded (highest-value mutation target)
findings.falsifiable_condition: Stryker on normalizeBpInput.ts produces surviving mutants on the shape-branching (lines 4-29), confirming the existing tests do not pin the heuristic.
findings.evidence: ≥6 implicit branches and two 'first-entry' fallbacks (lines 9-10, 21-29); never mutation-tested. This is where RISK-linker-002 would be confirmed or denied.

findings.title: deepMerge.ts — null/array/undefined/object branches, 0% mutation-graded
findings.falsifiable_condition: Stryker on deepMerge.ts produces surviving mutants on the null-erase (line 14) or array-replace (line 15) branches, confirming those destructive paths are not pinned.
findings.evidence: Four distinct override-type branches (undefined/null/array/object) drive config/draft/asset merges; never mutation-tested. deepMerge.test.ts exists but its adequacy is ungraded.

findings.title: namespaceBlueprints / resolveId — id-override and pre-namespaced branches, 0% mutation-graded
findings.falsifiable_condition: Stryker on linkerUtils.ts / utils/namespaces.ts produces surviving mutants on the explicit-id-wins branch (linkerUtils.ts:28-32) or the '::'-skip branch (namespaces.ts:2).
findings.evidence: The key-vs-id override and the namespacing-bypass (FOOTGUN-linker-003) are exactly the kind of conditional a weak test misses; never mutation-tested.

findings.title: Verified linker runtime model authored (new code-map section)
findings.note: The linker had no code_map.md section before this run. The verified model (pipeline, merge semantics, namespacing, serializer, gatekeeper) is in the atlas report §'Verified linker model', every claim anchored. Candidate for promotion into docs/manuals/code_map.md as a 7th section in a later pass. Informational — not a remediation item.
